name: Slovenia: participant-facing document QC
item_format: Each result records the item id, the outcome, a short rationale and evidence (quoted passage and source locator) or an explicit gap.

items.check: Protocol number, EU trial number, sponsor, full title, short title, investigational product, comparator and study population are consistent across every document.
The document is in Slovenian and uses correct clinical terminology rather than an unreviewed literal translation.
The document has a clear title, population, version number and date.
Randomisation, blinding, placebo or comparator use, treatment assignment and rescue treatment are explained accurately.
Visit counts, treatment duration, follow-up, sample volumes, imaging, questionnaires, device use, contraception and participant responsibilities match the protocol and schedule of activities.
Procedures deleted from the protocol are removed and procedures participants will experience are added.
Research-only procedures are distinguished from standard care.
Inclusion and exclusion points that participants must understand (contraception, prohibited medicines, washout, donation restrictions, driving, fasting, lifestyle requirements) match the protocol.
Foreseeable risks match the current Investigator's Brochure, protocol, product information and approved risk controls.
Stopping rules and reasons the investigator or sponsor may end participation are stated.
Withdrawal text is aligned with protocol safety follow-up and data-handling plans.
Compensation, expense reimbursement and treatment for injury match the financial (SI-P1) and insurance (SI-O1) documents.
Site contact names, roles, addresses and telephone numbers are verified against the current site file.
The Slovenian protocol synopsis covers the nationally required content and does not contradict the PIS (SI-D1-SYNOPSIS).
items.applies_when: document is an L1 information sheet

items.check: Main participation consent is distinct from optional future research, optional genetic testing, optional contact and pregnancy-partner follow-up.
Refusing an optional activity does not appear to prevent main-trial participation when the activity is not required.
The document states who signs it and when.
The application-stage blank form is free of participant, legal-representative, witness and interviewer signatures.
Space is provided for the participant's or representative's name, signature and date and for the person conducting the consent interview.
Where an impartial witness may be used, the approved form includes the witness statement, name, signature and date.
The person receives adequate time, an opportunity to ask questions and a signed and dated copy.
Re-consent triggers are stated for material new information, adulthood, regained capacity and newly proposed optional use.

The consent statements cover: written and oral information received and understood; questions asked and answered satisfactorily; enough time to decide; voluntariness; right to withdraw without giving a reason and without harm to ordinary care; agreement to the defined trial procedures; injury and insurance information understood; signed and dated copy received.
The package covers every population in the protocol and CTIS application (population × document table; every inclusion pathway has a document set).
Healthy volunteers: absence or uncertainty of therapeutic benefit, payment, burden, confinement, restrictions and reproductive risk are explained.

Minors: parent or legal-representative information and consent plus age-appropriate information and assent; the Slovenian 15-year threshold (own agreement from 15) and re-consent at adulthood are accounted for.
Adults unable to consent: legal-representative documents and information suited to the participant's capacity.
Emergency enrolment: the protocol and Part II documents address every Article 35 condition and the subsequent consent process.
Participant able to consent but unable to write: interpreter support is distinguished from the impartial-witness procedure.
Pregnancy follow-up: the pregnant participant is separated from a pregnant partner who is not a trial participant.
Optional future use: main-trial data and samples are separated from secondary purposes.
The controller or joint-controller arrangement is identified accurately.
Informed consent to participate is not equated with the GDPR legal basis for every processing operation.
Data categories, purposes, recipients, access to source records, coding, transfers, safeguards, retention and participant rights are explained.
The authorities, monitors, auditors and ethics bodies that may inspect records, and why, are stated.
International transfer wording matches actual destinations and safeguards.
No promise of complete anonymity when data remain coded or pseudonymised.
No promise of deletion when legally required safety and trial-integrity records must remain.
Withdrawal wording is aligned with the data-protection statement (SI-R1) and the protocol.
Optional future processing has its own clear legal and consent analysis.
Required and optional sample collections are listed separately.
Sample type, volume, frequency, analysis, genetic testing, storage, location, transfers, retention and destruction match the protocol and laboratory plan.
States whether samples are identified, coded, pseudonymised or irreversibly anonymised.
Explains whether individual or incidental findings may be returned.
Future research has a defined scope that a person can understand.
A separate refusal and withdrawal route is provided for optional future use.
No promise to destroy material already used, anonymised or included in completed analyses when that cannot be achieved.
The participant text is aligned with the CTIS biological-sample compliance document (SI-S1).
The cover letter is in Slovenian (SI-B1-COVER).
The protocol synopsis is in Slovenian and contains the items listed in Article 10 of the national implementing regulation (SI-D1-SYNOPSIS).
Every participant-facing item is in Slovenian.
The PIS is short, clear, respectful, empathetic and understandable to a lay reader (KME RS guidance).
Includes procedures, duration, benefits, risks, privacy, data access and retention, results availability, voluntariness, withdrawal, alternatives, safety and local contacts.
Insurance for trial-related injury is described consistently with the proof of sponsor and investigator liability cover (SI-O1).
The relevant investigator and national participant-rights contact routes are included with current official details.
Where teratogenic risk exists: written pregnancy and fetal-risk information, contraception instructions and the applicable signed acknowledgment are included.
For minors aged 15 or older: their own agreement is included in addition to legal-representative consent.
The PIS, ICF, assent, partner consent and optional-use forms submitted in CTIS are blank.
Signature blocks match the approved consent pathway and do not add an inappropriate signer.
Printed names, roles, signatures and dates are provided for where required during conduct.
Two signed copies of the consent form are provided for during conduct, one for the participant and one for the trial archive (KME RS).
Version and date match in the filename, footer, CTIS record, document list and translated file.
Tracked changes, comments, hidden text, unresolved fields and drafting notes are removed from clean files ([bracket] notes, italic notes, '...........' gaps, yellow form labels).
A traceable translation and review record is preserved.
Every cross-reference points to the correct document and section.
Headings answer participant questions.
Paragraphs and sentences are short.
Lists are used only where they make procedures or risks easier to understand.
Clinical, genetic and data-protection terms are defined.
Font size, spacing, contrast, page breaks, tables and signature-page legibility are checked.
Probabilities are explained in plain language with consistent denominators.
No coercive, reassuring, promotional or liability-waiving language.
The Slovenian text has been reviewed by a competent native-language clinical reviewer.
Only the versions intended for assessment are uploaded, in the correct CTIS categories.
The English scientific version of endpoint-related patient-facing documents is aligned with the Slovenian translation according to the current EU Q&A.
The version 2.0 recruitment and informed consent procedure template is used for new Part II submissions from 1 September 2026, and K1 matches the document pathways.
The document inventory is reconciled with the Slovenia Part II document checklist.
